_comment: Radial-breathing-mode <-> diameter relations, omega = A/d + B, with d in nm
There is no single correct (A, B). The RBM frequency of a given tube depends
on its environment: a tube in a bundle is stiffened by van der Waals contact
with its neighbours, a surfactant-wrapped tube less so, a suspended tube not
at all. Published A values span 215-248 and B spans 0-27, and choosing the
wrong pair biases every diameter by up to 10 %.
So this file offers the standard parameterisations side by side and the code
makes the user choose one, reports which was used, and can show the spread
across all of them as an honest uncertainty. 'environment' says what sample
each was calibrated on; use the one that matches yours.

parameterisations.label: Haces / polvo (A=234, B=10)
parameterisations.source: Jorio et al., Phys. Rev. B 65 (2002) 155412; Kuzmany et al., Eur. Phys. J. B 22 (2001) 307
parameterisations.notes: The workhorse for bundled material. The +10 cm-1 offset is the van der Waals stiffening from neighbouring tubes; it is NOT a fitting fudge, and dropping it on bundled samples overestimates diameters.

parameterisations.label: Tubos aislados sobre SiO2 (A=248, B=0)
parameterisations.environment: Individual SWCNTs on an oxidised silicon substrate
parameterisations.source: Jorio et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 86 (2001) 1118
parameterisations.notes: Calibrated against resonant Raman on isolated tubes with (n,m) assigned from the Kataura plot. Use for CVD-grown isolated tubes, not for powder.

parameterisations.label: Bandow (A=223.75, B=0)
parameterisations.source: Bandow et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 80 (1998) 3779
parameterisations.notes: One of the earliest calibrations, derived from a force-constant model.

parameterisations.label: Araujo, SWCNT en SDS (A=227, correccion de entorno)
parameterisations.source: Araujo et al., Phys. Rev. B 77 (2008) 241403(R)
parameterisations.notes: Uses omega = (A/d) * sqrt(1 + C_e d^2) rather than A/d + B, with C_e = 0.05789 nm^-2 for SDS. The multiplicative form keeps the pristine-tube frequency A/d and puts all the environment in one term.

parameterisations.label: Paredes internas de DWCNT (A=204, B=27)
parameterisations.environment: Inner tubes of double-walled CNTs and peapod-derived tubes
parameterisations.source: Milnera et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 84 (2000) 1324; Pfeiffer et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 90 (2003) 225501
parameterisations.notes: Inner tubes are shielded by the outer wall and sit in a different mechanical environment; using a bundle parameterisation on them underestimates their diameter.

wall_spacing_note: Measured wall-to-wall separations in DWCNTs run 0.33-0.36 nm, wider than graphite's 0.335 nm because of curvature. Two RBM peaks whose diameters differ by 2 x (0.33-0.36) = 0.66-0.72 nm are a candidate inner/outer pair.
wall_spacing_source: Pfeiffer et al., Phys. Rev. B 72 (2005) 161404; Hirschmann et al., ACS Nano 7 (2013) 2205

g_band_splitting._comment: omega(G-) = omega(G+) - C / d^2, an INDEPENDENT diameter estimate that needs no RBM. Useful for spectra whose low-frequency cutoff hides the RBM region entirely.
g_band_splitting.source: Jorio et al., Phys. Rev. B 65 (2002) 155412
g_band_splitting.notes: The metallic constant is larger because the softening of the metallic G- has an extra electron-phonon contribution on top of curvature. Applying the semiconducting constant to a metallic tube overestimates the diameter by about 30 %.

chirality._comment: Geometry of a (n,m) tube. a = sqrt(3) * a_CC is the graphene lattice constant.
chirality.metallicity_rule: (n - m) mod 3 == 0 -> metallic (armchair n=m truly metallic; other (n-m)%3==0 tubes open a small curvature gap of a few tens of meV and are called quasi-metallic)
chirality.source: Saito, Dresselhaus & Dresselhaus, Physical Properties of Carbon Nanotubes (1998)
